pencereler.0-5: USAir 1016 failed because microburst wind shear on approach. It burst into flames, and
pencereler.5-12: thirty seven people were killed. A thunderstorm sat over the airport. The tower issued a wind shear warning, but
pencereler.12-20: on a different frequency. On final approach, a microburst hit the jet. The crew tried to go around, but the plane kept
pencereler.20-30: sinking. An alert system error also delayed its warning. Wind shear detection and crew training were improved.

segmentler.metin: USAir Flight 1016 crashed into trees and a house near Charlotte.
It took only a microburst during a go-around in a thunderstorm.
So how could a microburst during a go-around in a thunderstorm do this?
The answer is microburst wind shear on approach, with alerts that came late or on another frequency — and it is why wind shear detection and crew recognition training were improved.
